basics.name: Clint Andrew Hall
basics.summary:
I'm a Principal Engineer and engineering leader focused on user interfaces. I work to make the web beautiful, both on its surface and beneath.

Today I help steer Global UX at Elastic: the EUI design system, Shared UX, and the cross-cutting experiences every Elastic application is built on. I set technical direction across teams, coordinate work that spans organizations, and still ship significant code myself — from TypeScript and React architecture down to the CSS and accessibility details most people never see.

I'm at my best where design and engineering meet. I respect designers' craft and build alongside them, and when I have an idea I'd rather prove it with a working demo than describe it — code wins arguments.

I'm affable and good-natured, yet results-driven and competitive, and I've led and worked within distributed teams for more than a decade, at Facebook and at Elastic.

principles.detail: When I wanted to prove every Kibana illustration could theme itself from a single file, I didn't write a proposal — I built the proof-of-concept. A working demo ends the debate.

principles.statement: No wall between design and engineering.
principles.detail: I respect and expect designers' craft, and I build alongside them. My team at Elastic was built to bridge design and engineering — turning consistency across our products into shared infrastructure, not a handoff over a fence.
Semantics, keyboard paths, and screen-reader support aren't a checklist I bolt on at the end — they're where I start. This site included.

principles.statement: AI is a tool, not a magician.
principles.detail: Years ago I gave a TEDx talk on why technology sold as “magic” leaves people worse off. AI is no exception: I direct it, review every line, and own the result. The judgment stays mine.

resume.summary: Principal Engineer and Tech Lead focused on UI architecture, design systems and accessibility. Sets technical direction for Elastic's EUI design system and Shared UX while still shipping significant code, bridging design and engineering by proving ideas with working code.

highlights: One of two Tech Leads for Elastic's Application Experience org, directing Global UX: the EUI design system, Shared UX, and Search and ML experiences.
Co-founded the Shared UX team to make consistency across Elastic's solutions a product: shared components, services and application chrome.
Co-created the Kibana Workspace proof-of-concept, funded as a cross-team project and the reference for Kibana's new Workspace Chrome layout and visual refresh.
Designed the developer API and session model for EUI's Flyout System (EUI v111), now used by Kibana Core and across Discover, APM, SLOs and Alerting.
Built Content List, a composable replacement for Kibana's listing pages; migrated Graph, Maps and Annotations, and another team adopted it independently.
Shipped @kbn/one-navigation, letting other Elastic web apps reuse Kibana's navigation, and AI Assistant iconography adopted by Observability, Search and Security.
As Area Lead, took Kibana Canvas from beta to GA over ten releases, then led the Presentation team; introduced TypeScript, i18n and Storybook to Canvas.
Rebuilt Facebook Events on the web: a new Events Dashboard in Relay and Permalink across desktop and mobile web.
Converted the Composer to React and built the new Share Dialog on top of it.
Built a React messaging inbox for the Help Center and the Open Graph Share dialog for Facebook Platform.
Improved accessibility for screen-reader users, including a new way to “see” photos; rebuilt OAuth dialogs and social plugins for developers.
Cerner's first Web Evangelist, advising product teams on semantics, accessibility, progressive enhancement and responsible use of CSS and JavaScript.
Invented the Web Bootstrapper, a patented technique that lets one semantic site adapt to any device; presented it at WWW and W4A.

publications.name: Web Presentation Layer Bootstrapping for Accessibility and Performance
publications.summary: In this paper, I present the Web Bootstrapper, a technique that allows a developer to write a single site while still providing multiple experiences, or "skins," without altering source or running costly client-side code. It is a process by which an accurate collection of only those static resources and metadata necessary for a unique experience be delivered passively, by the most performant means possible.

work.name: Elastic
work.position: Principal Engineer & Tech Lead, Application Experience
work.summary:
A June 2026 reorganization named me one of two Tech Leads for Elastic's Application Experience organization, with my focus on Global UX.  Global UX brings together the Shared UX and Elastic User Interface (EUI) teams with our Search experiences and Machine Learning (ML) UX — the shared foundation and cross-cutting experiences that the rest of the org's solutions are built on.

I lead this group through a technology lens: setting technical direction across its teams, coordinating projects that span organizations, and consulting with the other tech leaders across Application Experience and the wider company.  As a Principal Engineer I also contribute significant and moonshot work directly, and continue to champion consistency, accessibility, and a durable design system as the foundation for every Elastic application.

custom.tagline: My scope grew with the reorg — one of two Tech Leads under Application Experience, now steering a broader Global UX: Shared UX, EUI, Search experiences, and ML UX.

highlights: [kibana/268796](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/268796): Leading the move of Kibana's listing pages to Content List — Graph, Maps and Annotations migrated so far, with the Alerting v2 team adopting it independently.

work.name: Elastic
work.position: Principal Engineer & Tech Lead, Global Experience
work.summary:
Global Experience is the umbrella for the common experiences across Kibana — home pages, application chrome, content navigation, and the shared components every Elastic application starts from.  It comprises two teams: the Elastic User Interface (EUI) — a design system of patterns and guidelines embodying the Elastic brand, paired with the component library that follows them — and Shared UX, the group of product, design, and engineering specialists making consistency in Kibana a product by providing common UX infrastructure like chrome, modals, and state management.

I lead Global Experience through a technology lens as its Tech Lead, and was named Principal Engineer along the way.  I coordinate technical efforts across the group, represent it across Kibana and the wider Application Experience organization, and consult with tech leaders throughout Elastic.  Our scope spans navigation, layout and the home page, shared components, accessibility, the EUI design system, and the platform's file and ML/AI-connector experiences.

custom.tagline: Principal Engineer for Global Experience — the umbrella over EUI and Shared UX, owning the chrome, navigation, and design system every Elastic app is built on.

highlights: [kibana/212002](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/212002): Co-built the Kibana Workspace proof-of-concept that was ratified into a funded, cross-team Workspace Chrome project; its phase-2 exploration ([kibana/235808](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/235808)) became the reference for the sidebar and visual-refresh epics.
[kibana/242734](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/242734): Created `@kbn/one-navigation`, an external package that lets other Elastic web apps share Kibana's navigation.

[eui/8939](https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/8939): Authored the developer API and session model for EUI's Flyout System, shipped in EUI v111 and now used through Kibana Core's `openSystemFlyout` and across Discover, APM, SLOs and Alerting.
[kibana/247778](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/247778): Designed Content List, a composable replacement for Kibana's monolithic `TableListView` listing pages.
[kibana/203879](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/203879): Created the shared AI Assistant icon, avatar and beacon components, adopted across Observability, Search and Security.
Founded Horizons, Global Experience's bottom-up R&D track for exploratory work like theme-adaptive illustrations, code sharing between web apps, and visual regression testing.

work.name: Elastic
work.summary:
I'm the Tech Lead for Shared User Experience (UX) for the Application Experience organization at Elastic.  The team was conceived by myself and other leaders to bridge the gap between design and the myriad of solutions that comprise our Application Experience organization.  Our mission is to make consistency across our solutions a product.  My role is leading the team through a technology lens, coordinating projects, and consulting with other tech leaders across Elastic.

My team is responsible for creating, maintaining and supporting shared UX infrastructure, like components, hooks and services.  We also promote patterns from our design organizations, fostering adoption through evangelism and codifying them in our infrastructure.  We're also responsible for unique UX solutions, driving our projects across organizations, and consulting with teams to deliver consistent experiences.

custom.tagline: Leading a team that bridges design and the many solutions across Elastic's Application Experience org — making consistency itself a product.

I became the Area Lead for this new team, coordinating efforts between these products and the rest of Kibana.  I continued my previous responsibilities, this time on a larger scale: overseeing and coordinating technical efforts, representing the team across the org, and contributing significant or moonshot enhancements.

work.name: Elastic
work.summary:
In October of 2018, I accepted a role with [Elastic](https://www.elastic.co) to work on [Kibana](https://www.elastic.co/kibana), specifically a new, ground-breaking beta plugin called [Canvas](https://www.elastic.co/what-is/kibana-canvas).  Soon after, I was named the new Area Lead.  I was responsible for overseeing and coordinating our technical efforts, representing the team across the org, and contributing significant or moonshot enhancements.

During my tenure I directed project efforts for 1 major and 9 minor releases, including the General Availability (GA) release of Canvas from beta.  I introduced a number of technologies and architecture approaches that stabilized and enhanced the plugin, and oversaw migration of valuable bespoke technology to the Kibana ecosystem, (e.g. [`expressions`](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/current/kibana-expressions-plugin.html)).
highlights: [kibana/31734](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/31734): Significant React performance investigation.
[kibana/35087](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/35087): Introduced Typescript.
[kibana/36252](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/36252): Introduced internationalization architecture.
[kibana/38850](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/38850): Introduced [Storybook](https://storybook.js.org) for rapid development and testing.
[kibana/46278](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/46278): Built novel means of embedding Canvas Workpads.

custom.tagline: Directed Canvas from beta to GA; introduced TypeScript, i18n, and Storybook to a ground-breaking plugin.

work.name: Facebook
work.summary:
When I first moved to the NYC Facebook office, I joined the Composer team for a "hack-a-quarter", converting the Composer to React, and then worked on the Share Dialog.

Eventually Events found themselves with a large number of React and Relay projects, so I rejoined my former team remotely. I built the new Events Dashboard and Permalink, and implemented many "under the hood" improvements.
highlights: New Events Dashboard for desktop in Relay.
New Events Dashboard for the mobile site in XHP.
New Events Permalink for all web surfaces in XHP.
New React + Flux Composer, and the new Share Dialog using that component.
New 'Minutiae' controls — the structured data (Photos, Activity, Tags) found in Composer.

custom.tagline: Converted Composer to React, built the Share Dialog, and shipped the Events Dashboard and Permalink in Relay.

work.name: Facebook

There I worked on the Protect and Care team, building a new Help Center messaging inbox in React, and implemented the Open Graph Share dialog for FB Platform in XHP.
highlights: New Help Center Inbox for desktop in React.
New "How-to" panels for the Help Center.
New Platform Share Dialog for mobile and desktop in XHP.

custom.tagline: Built a React messaging inbox for Protect & Care, and the Open Graph Share dialog for FB Platform.

work.name: Facebook
work.summary:
I joined Facebook in 2012 as a User Interface Engineer (UIE) on the Mobile Core Web team.  I then joined the Accessibility team to help make Facebook more useful to everyone on the web.

After several hackathons involving Events, I joined the team full time to rewrite the web experiences on both the mobile and main website.

Afterwards, I spent some time with the Platform team, reworking a number of different web flows, like OAuth, and embeddable components like Share, Hashtags and Topics.
highlights: New OAuth flow dialogs for developers using Facebook.
New Share, Hashtags and Topics plugins for developers.
New mobile web experience for the Events Dashboard and Permalink.
Improved the Accessibility of Facebook, including a new way to "see" photos.
New core components for mobile web for product teams.

custom.tagline: Joined on Mobile Core Web and Accessibility — including a new way to "see" photos — before rewriting Events across web.

"Proscenium", an experimental technique of compiling templates in JS libraries for isomorphic rendering.

work.name: Cerner Corporation
work.summary: For several years I was a Software Architect for Healthe, enforcing cross-browser compatibility, semantic markup and accessibility, developing CSS layouts and advanced JavaScript controls, and conducting platform research.  I would also prototype HTML code based on paper designs, allowing the team to communicate intent to clients, stakeholders, usability and engineers.
highlights: Championed a comprehensive browser-agnostic web philosophy, massively improving accessibility, portability and performance.
Invented the 'Web Bootstrapper', a patented technology that allowed semantic web pages to adapt to the heuristics of any device, dynamically.
Consultant and mentor to teams and engineers on web technology and development.

custom.tagline: Invented the patented Web Bootstrapper and set a browser-agnostic web practice for Healthe, improving accessibility, portability and performance.

work.name: Cerner Corporation
work.summary: For several years I worked on the ePrescribing (eRx) and Community Health Record (CHR) solutions for treating Medicare populations in several states. I would interpret functional requirements into a coherent user interface and visual design.
highlights: Proposed and built the "New Navigation" project, which was a radical redesign of the UI based on usability studies and feedback from sales.
Novel architecture pattern discarding JSPs in favor of full modules of aggregate presentation components, adding entire workflows to any WAR using standard J2EE and Struts configurations.
Mentored software engineers and other architects in semantic markup practices and prudent Javascript.

custom.tagline: Proposed and built a usability-driven redesign of the ePrescribing and Community Health Record interfaces.

work.name: Cerner Corporation
work.summary: When I joined Cerner, I took on the role of Presentation Layer Developer for the "Web Experience" solution, specifically Order Management. I would design, document, and develop the UI for order placement, drug catalog browsing, and proactive interaction checking and alerting.
highlights: Reusable, component-based rendering system which resulted in an 80% reduction in markup in JSPs, as well as sharing between solutions.
Subject matter expert for most presentation layer technologies, and reviewed most of that code from my (and other) teams.  I ended up teaching a few courses for new associates.

custom.tagline: Built a reusable, component-based rendering system for Order Management that cut JSP markup by 80%.
